text: Barded Warhorse
An armoured Imperial charger, trained not to shy at spellfire.
Imperial Pegasus
A winged Imperial steed that carries him over the enemy line.
Disc of Tzeentch
A floating daemon disc of Tzeentch. He does not talk about what he paid for it.
Carmine Dragon
A blood-red dragon of the old Empire. It has seen more endings than he has.
Staff and Sword

A walking staff for his spells and a plain Imperial blade for anything that gets too close.\\n\\nHis default weapon, which he always has. Switch back to it with the Change Loadout button in his character panel.
Sword and Shield
A sword and a knight's shield. He leaves the staff behind to stand in the front line.\\n\\nUnlocks this weapon for the Advisor. Switch to it with the Change Loadout button in his character panel.
Sword and Bow
A hunting bow and a short blade. He was a fair shot long before he became a wizard.\\n\\nUnlocks this weapon for the Advisor. Switch to it with the Change Loadout button in his character panel.
Greatsword

A two-handed Imperial greatsword, far heavier than a wizard should carry. He swings it well enough.\\n\\nUnlocks this weapon for the Advisor. Switch to it with the Change Loadout button in his character panel.
Glaive

A long Cathayan glaive built to cut a horse out from under its rider, with a short sword at his hip for close work.\\n\\nUnlocks this weapon for the Advisor. Switch to it with the Change Loadout button in his character panel.
Iron Hand

No weapon at all. He fights with open hands and the weight of a forge behind every blow, the way the dragon-blooded lords of Cathay do.\\n\\nUnlocks this weapon for the Advisor. Switch to it with the Change Loadout button in his character panel.
Default Actions
The hero actions he always has: Scouting, Scout Settlement and Boost Income.
Apex: Archmage

He has studied every lore there is across many lives, and all of it is within reach now.\\n\\nEach turn his army gains one random cataclysm spell, a memory of how some world ended.\\n\\nLocks the Polymath and every other Apex.
Apex: The Last Sword
In one ending he was the last man still fighting. He trains as if it will happen again.\\n\\nLocks the Polymath and every other Apex.
Master of Arms

In other lives he mastered each of these weapons in turn. Now he no longer has to choose.\\n\\nStacks with any other Apex or the Polymath.\\n\\nWhat it does follows the weapon in his hands. Use Change Loadout to see the new effects.
Apex: Power Behind Thrones
Across many lives he has advised kings, emperors and warlords. Every court he serves runs better for it.\\n\\nLocks the Polymath and every other Apex.
Army I: Drill
The soldiers near him copy how he stands and moves, and fight better for it.\\n\\nWhat it does follows the weapon in his hands. Use Change Loadout to see the new effects.
Army II: Formation
He sets out the line to suit the way he fights.\\n\\nWhat it does follows the weapon in his hands. Use Change Loadout to see the new effects.
Army III: Last Stand
Hold here. I have seen what happens to the ones who run.\\n\\nWhat it does follows the weapon in his hands. Use Change Loadout to see the new effects.
Army IV: Every Banner
Every army he marched with in other lives taught him something. Now his men learn all of it.\\n\\nWhat it does follows the weapon in his hands. Use Change Loadout to see the new effects.
Art I: Stance
Get your feet right. Everything else follows from the feet.\\n\\nWhat it does follows the weapon in his hands. Use Change Loadout to see the new effects.
Art II: Edge
With his footing settled, he learns where each blow does the most harm.\\n\\nWhat it does follows the weapon in his hands. Use Change Loadout to see the new effects.
Art III: Flow
Attack and guard stop being separate moves. Each one runs straight into the next.\\n\\nWhat it does follows the weapon in his hands. Use Change Loadout to see the new effects.
Art IV: Ending
Every fight has a last blow. Make sure it is yours.\\n\\nWhat it does follows the weapon in his hands. Use Change Loadout to see the new effects.
A Host of His Own
His soldiers fight the way he taught them, whatever weapon he carries that day.
A Style of His Own
Six weapons, six teachers, and a lifetime with each. He has taken the best of all of them and made it his own.
Arcane Ward
A standing ward he renews each morning. Blows that should land often slide off.
Deep Quiver
He carries more arrows than most archers think worth the weight.
Duelling Wards
A small ward on his blade and wrist turns aside blows that would otherwise land.
Blade of the Winds
In another life the Winds themselves guided his sword. He still fights that way, and the men near him fight better for it.
Storm of Needles
He shoots faster and further than ever, and the archers near him learn to keep up.
Unbroken
He has been the last man left on the field more than once. He no longer knows how to run, and the men near him take heart from it.
Flesh Remembers
His body takes well to healing magic and recovers more from it.
Ironbound Sleeves
Iron bands sewn into his sleeves let him beat a blade aside and strike back in the same move.
Light Along the Line
He spreads his magic shield across every unit in his army.
The Long Breath
Pace yourself. The battle will still be there in an hour.
Long Sight
He picks out targets at ranges where most archers would not bother to draw.
Mended Shell
When his magic shield breaks, it comes back sooner and stronger.
Piercing Shot
Aim for the buckle. That is where the armour ends.
Practised Aim
Endless practice with the bow. He shoots harder and nocks the next arrow sooner.
Shell of Light
A shield of pure magic hangs in the air around him and soaks up blows.
Spell and Steel
He fights with a sword in one hand and casts with the other, and each makes the other stronger.
Steady Hands
Slowly. A rushed spell is how the world ended last time.
Steel in the Weave
He puts a little of the Winds behind every cut, and it bites deeper.
Veteran's Hide
Old scars and well-worn armour. Blows that would cut a younger man leave him bruised.
Warded Mind
He has been on the wrong end of enough spells to know how to shrug one off.
Warden of the Shell
He can mend the magic barriers of the men around him in the middle of a fight.
Weight of the Charge
He learned to charge from a knight, and hits the enemy line with his full weight.
A Corrupting Presence
He has learned to carry every kind of corruption at once. Wherever he stays, all of them spread faster.
Spread Chaos Corruption
He carries the taint of the Dark Gods with him, and the land around him sours.
Spread Khorne Corruption
Skulls on the roadsides, blood in the wells. The Blood God's mark follows him.
Spread Nurgle Corruption
Flies, rot and slow fevers follow him. The Plague God's gifts spread where he walks.
Spread Skaven Corruption
Warpstone dust in the grain and scratching in the walls. The Horned Rat's taint follows him.
Spread Slaanesh Corruption
Strange music, sweet smells and restless dreams follow him. The Dark Prince's touch spreads where he goes.
Spread Tzeentch Corruption
Things shift and change where he passes. The Changer's mark spreads in his wake.
Spread Vampiric Corruption
Graves stir and the nights grow longer where he stays. The taint of undeath spreads from him.
The Taint Remembered
He has watched every kind of corruption take hold of a land, and learned how to keep it out. In his own provinces it takes hold more slowly.
Assassinate
He picks out the enemy agent who will cause the most trouble later, and deals with them now.
Assassinate Lord
Even generals have to sleep somewhere. He knows where.
Assault Garrison
He slips into the settlement and strikes at the garrison before it can form up.
Assault Units
He strikes the enemy camp at night and leaves several units bloodied by morning.
Block Army
Cut ropes, lamed horses and lost orders. The enemy army goes nowhere.
Boost Income
His advice on taxes and trade puts more gold in the treasury.
Cleanse Corruption
He finds the taint early and burns it out before it can take hold.
Damage Building
A fire in the right storehouse can do more damage than a whole army.
Damage Walls
He weakens the mortar and cracks the stone, so the walls come down faster when the siege starts.
The Banner Remembered
He has watched armies fall apart in other lives and learned why. His stay fed, paid and in good heart.
A Hand in Every Pocket
He has run spy networks across many lives. Doors open for him, secrets reach him, and enemies walk into his ambushes.
The Lamp in the Window
Across many lives he has helped so many people that his name is welcome everywhere. Towns grow calmer and richer where he passes.
Forager's Eye
He knows what is worth taking from a beaten army, and where they hid it.
Hinder Replenishment
He spoils their supplies and turns away their recruits, so their losses stay unfilled.
Increase Mobility
He clears the road ahead and finds the quickest route for the army.
Increase Trade
He knows which roads will stay safe and which ships will come home.
Pathfinder
He leads the army by paths the maps do not show.
Replenish Troops
He knows where to find fresh recruits and how to bring them into the ranks quickly.
Scavenge
After the battle he makes sure nothing useful is left lying on the field.
Scouting
He goes ahead of the army and comes back with what is waiting there.
Spread Public Order
Be glad of what you have. I have seen the alternative.
Steal Technology
He reads their scholars' notes and brings home the parts worth having.
Stimulate Growth
He knows which crops will fail and which fields will yield, and the province grows.
Students in Every Court
Many captains and wizards learned from him in other lives. New recruits arrive already knowing his lessons.
Training
He drills the troops himself, and they learn faster for it.
Wound
I do not need him dead. I need him out of the way for a while.
The Long Patience
Once every other skill is learned, the rest of his time goes into slow, steady practice.
Arcane Conduit
He opens himself to the Winds and draws them in faster than a wizard should.
Deep Reserves
Long practice lets him gather and hold more of the Winds than most wizards can.
Conduit Unbound
He no longer fights the Winds for every drop of power. He lets them flow through him and spends them freely.
Weave Beyond Sight
Lifetimes of study let him read the Winds more clearly than any living mage, and see further by them.
The Well Remembers
Across many lives he has drawn on the same deep well of magic. It comes to him easily now.
Hex of Misfire
He curses the enemy's casters, so their spells cost more and go wrong more often.
Open Channel
The Winds of Magic gather around him faster than around most wizards.
Overcast Discipline
Push a spell past its limit, then let go before it bites back.
Quick Recitation
He has spoken these incantations so often that the words come without thought.
Quiet Mind
With a calm mind, he can ready his next spell sooner.
Second Wind
He has learned to store more of the Winds for the long fights.
Sharper Weave
He keeps tight hold of every thread of a spell, so very little goes wrong.
Spellweaver's Focus
He keeps his mind on the spell, whatever is happening around him.
Steady Cadence
He casts to a steady rhythm of word and breath, and wastes less of the Winds on each spell.
Wider Weave
He learns to stretch the same Winds further, so each spell costs him less.
Memory: Calm Voice
He stopped being afraid of anything a long time ago, and the soldiers near him can tell.
Memory: The Ending of Drowning
In one ending the sea rose over the walls. He learned to keep his head and his shield up while everything else went under.\\n\\nLocks the other Endings.
Memory: The Ending of Fire
In one ending the sky burned for nine days. His blade still carries the heat.\\n\\nLocks the other Endings.
Memory: The Ending of Hunger
In one ending the granaries were empty before the first battle. He learned to wear his enemies down the way hunger wears down a city.\\n\\nLocks the other Endings.
Memory: The Ending of Plague
In one ending the cities emptied one by one from sickness. Some of it stayed with him.\\n\\nLocks the other Endings.
Memory: The Ending of Silence
In one ending the enemy came without a sound, and whole armies vanished. He learned to shake men before the blow lands.\\n\\nLocks the other Endings.
Memory: Every Mistake Already Made
I have made every mistake there is to make. I do not plan to make them twice.
Memory: Old Lessons
He learned every lesson the hard way, many times over. Teaching them, and picking up new ones, comes easily.
Memory: Seen the End
In another life he watched this army walk into an ambush. He reads the ground ahead much more closely now.
Memory: The Weight of Years
He has died before. He did not care for it, and he takes more killing now.
Polymath: Everything, Again

In different lives he was a swordsman, a sorcerer, a spy and a steward. This time he means to be all four.\\n\\nA discipline counts once he knows 5 of its skills: Arts, Memory, Magic (learned spells count) and Hero work. Every discipline that counts makes every lord and hero in his faction stronger, and all four make them the strongest they can be.\\n\\nLocks every Apex.
